tools.name: catalog_get
tools.description: Use this for questions about Carrel features, images or the development environment. Get exact service.version, installed images, size presets, VM/CT restrictions, MiB/GiB units and supported capabilities together. No deployment preview needed to discover support. Images include environment, default_size and default_swap_mb; minimal and development are distinct prepared images. Creation defaults: debian-13-minimal VM, 1 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM, 10 GiB disk, 1 GiB swap; it has SSH, cloud-init and Python, but no Node, Docker or compilers. For a prepared development VM use image=debian-13 or ubuntu-24.04 (default size=small: 2 vCPU/2 GiB/20 GiB). size=tiny is 1 vCPU/1 GiB/10 GiB; cpu, memory_mb and disk_gb override a preset. New CTs default to Debian 13, tiny, no swap; CTs do not support packages, runcmd, health_checks or nested_virt. ssh_key_add saves a key once for future creation. Default personal/project quota: 8 machines and 8 IPs, 8 vCPU, 16 GiB RAM, 100 GiB disk. Each SSH uses one of 10 tenant public ports, leaving two for extra TCP/UDP publications with eight machines; HTTPS domains use none. Stopped and paused machines keep their reservations. Resize needs quota and node capacity; disk only grows and owner SSH must grow the filesystem.

tools.name: machine_create
tools.description: Create one VM/CT directly when the user asks for a machine. Defaults: Debian 13 minimal VM, 1 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM, 10 GiB disk, 1 GiB swap. Supply an SSH public key inline or use saved keys. No discovery or preview call is required; admission checks run during creation. Waits up to 55 seconds and returns verified readiness and SSH details in operation.result; only call operation_get if still pending. dry_run=true is optional for preview requests. Use VMs for Docker, OVS, Mininet or databases. CTs do not support packages, runcmd, health_checks or nested_virt. Use deployment_apply for multiple machines, connections or publications. Use the known default public key only if saved keys are unavailable; do not scan unrelated SSH configuration. Successful summary omits quota tables; detail=full retrieves them. For local CLI clients, creation includes merging returned ssh_config while preserving existing entries, verifying its tenant-qualified alias with ssh -G, and presenting ssh_short. Use direct ssh only if client setup is unavailable, excluded or fails. Minimal has no Node, Docker or compilers. Choose image=debian-13 or ubuntu-24.04 for prepared development tools and default size=small (2 vCPU/2 GiB/20 GiB). Explicit size/resource fields override image defaults. CTs default to tiny with no swap. Choose larger resources for builds and Docker stacks.

image.description: Default VM: debian-13-minimal. Debian/Ubuntu development images remain available. CTs use debian-13 or ubuntu-24.04. Or "tenant:image:<name>" for one of this tenant's imported cloud images (image_import); the disk is at least the image's virtual size. ("tenant:<name>" still means the same.) tools.description: Publish HTTPS at <sub>.<tenant>.winlab.tw, or with name at a special domain the tenant was granted (domain_request): the granted name, or for a wildcard grant the catch-all *.<base> or one label under it. The gateway ends TLS and forwards plain HTTP with the original Host header, X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto; WebSockets pass through. tools.description: Send one webhook.test event to a webhook now and return the HTTP status it answered with. It changes nothing in Carrel, and runs outside the platform's write lock.

tools.name: function_deploy
tools.description: Deploy a container image as a function: it runs only while it has requests and sleeps without memory otherwise, waking from a snapshot in about 100 ms. The image must serve HTTP on its port. Each deploy builds a new version from the image (pulled anonymously; linux/amd64) and puts it live once its first answer below 500 arrives. Returns at once with state building; follow it with function_get and wait_seconds. A function keeps no state between instances.

image.description: Image reference in a registry that needs no credentials, such as ghcr.io/owner/app:1.2 or docker.io/library/nginx:1.27.

port.description: Port the image serves HTTP on.

instance.description: reuse: one instance serves requests until idle (web services, APIs). fresh: every request gets its own instance, destroyed after the answer (untrusted code, job runners).

idle_seconds.description: reuse: seconds without a request before the instance sleeps.

wake_path.description: Path the platform calls once after every wake, to reseed state kept in memory; every wake restores the same snapshot.

dry_run.description: Preview only: no resource writes or reservations (audit is recorded). Returns quota_before, delta, quota_after, requirements and ready_to_apply. No follow-up list/quota/key checks are needed to prove it made no changes.

tools.name: function_get
tools.description: Show one function: state (building, deployed, failed, not_deployed), the settings of its current version, its kept versions with build errors and sizes, and whether its function host is connected. With wait_seconds, waits up to 55 seconds while a build is in progress.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for completion; 0 returns the job at once.

tools.name: function_logs
tools.description: Read the end of a function's output: what its instances wrote to standard output and standard error, each line starting with the time it was written. The platform keeps the last 10 MB per function on its host. With build, reads the output of its builds instead, the place to look when a version failed. Asks the function host and waits up to 15 seconds for it.

since_seconds.description: Only lines written in the last this many seconds.

max_bytes.description: Return at most this many bytes from the end.

tools.name: function_env
tools.description: Set a function's environment variables without passing the values through tool arguments. Returns a single-use upload link valid for 15 minutes: run its upload line where the environment file is (UTF-8, one KEY=VALUE per line; whole-line # comments, export and one pair of quotes around a value are allowed; no inline comments, escapes or multi-line values). The values replace the whole environment, are kept encrypted, and a new version of the function builds with them; follow it with function_get and wait_seconds. A deploy keeps the environment; a rollback brings back the one its version was built with. clear builds a version without variables. function_get shows the variable names, never the values.

tools.name: function_registry
tools.description: Let a function pull its image from a private registry, without passing the token through tool arguments. Returns a single-use upload link valid for 15 minutes and an upload line that reads REGISTRY_USER and REGISTRY_TOKEN from the shell. The credentials are kept encrypted and sent only to that registry (default: the registry of the function's current image), when the function's host builds a version. Deploy after uploading. clear removes them. function_get shows the registry, never the credentials.

registry.description: Registry host, such as ghcr.io. Default: the registry of the function's current image.

tools.name: function_link
tools.description: Deploy a function on every push to a GitHub repository branch (PLAN 7.11). Returns workflow (commit to .github/workflows/carrel.yml): GitHub Actions builds the image, pushes it to ghcr.io and sends its digest to carrel with the job's OIDC token, so the repository holds no carrel secret. Each push builds a new version with the function's current settings and environment; deploy once with function_deploy first. Only the linked repository and branch, on push or workflow_dispatch, can deploy; with previews, each pull request from the repository itself also deploys to its own preview. clear unlinks and removes the previews.

previews.description: Also deploy each pull request from the repository itself to its own preview, pr-<number>-<function>, at https://pr-<number>-<function>.<tenant>.winlab.tw, removed when the pull request closes. A preview starts from the function's settings without its environment, schedules or registry credentials. At most 5 at once; they count against the functions and domains quota. Needs one push deploy first.

tools.name: function_schedule
tools.description: Add, replace or remove one cron schedule of a function. At each minute the expression matches in time_zone, the function's host sends GET path (POST with body as application/json when body is set) to the function with the header X-Carrel-Schedule: <name>, which outside requests can never carry. A run still going when its schedule comes round is skipped; minutes missed during an outage are not replayed. Each run's status goes to function_logs. function_get lists the schedules. At most 10 per function.

name.description: The schedule's name, unique within the function.

cron.description: 5 fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, with *, numbers, a-b ranges, lists and /steps, such as */5 * * * * or 0 9 * * 1-5.

time_zone.description: IANA zone such as UTC or Asia/Taipei.

body.description: Sent with POST; without it the request is a GET.

tools.name: deployment_plan

Set network_access=restricted on connection destinations to enforce isolation; tenant mode allows all tenant machines. Optional networks/attachments are advanced L2 experiments. Checks aggregate quota/capacity; missing SSH keys become requirements. No resource writes or reservations. This is the complete preview: apply the same specification once with deployment_apply when authorized; do not create each resource separately. Publications can reference existing machine names with no machines array. Use access to change an existing machine ingress mode, together with connections if needed. Preview explains lost or added connectivity; set access.confirm to its name when authorized. Machine defaults match machine_create: Debian 13 minimal, tiny (1 vCPU/1 GiB/10 GiB), 1 GiB swap. Development images debian-13 and ubuntu-24.04 default to small. Explicit size/resource fields override image defaults.

tools.name: operation_get
tools.description: Continue waiting for a pending operation with id, up to 55 seconds by default (zero for immediate status). No call is needed after a succeeded mutation. Without id, list the latest 50 tenant operations. Summary preserves next_action, failures, cleanup and pending reservation status; detail=full includes full accounting and identifiers. done is true once the operation has finished, whatever its state. Follow next_action, and poll no faster than poll_after_seconds.

tools.name: operation_retry
tools.description: Resume a failed operation using its original allocation and durable checkpoints. A rolled-back deployment gets a fresh attempt; cleanup_failed retries cleanup first. Does not repeat a succeeded operation. Follow next_action first. revise_request operations keep their original arguments and are not requeued.

tools.name: operation_cancel
tools.description: Cancel an operation that has changed nothing yet: one still queued, or one waiting its turn behind another job. It ends failed with error code cancelled and frees its queue place; operation_retry runs it again. A running plugin operation is asked to cancel: it ends failed with code cancelled, or answers conflict and keeps running if the plugin refuses or cannot stop it. Anything else that has started changing resources answers conflict with its state.

dry_run.description: Check that the operation can be cancelled without cancelling it.

instructions:
WinLab machines through MCP. Call the tool for the task directly with the known machine name; whoami, catalog_get, quota_get and capacity_get are not prerequisites. Use machine_list only to list or for an ambiguous target. Omit tenant for personal resources. Do not use operator memories, runbooks, hypervisor access or unrelated SSH inspection. dry_run previews; wait_seconds 0 returns the job at once. Toolsets: core, machines (snapshot_*, machine_freeze/thaw), network (domain_*, port_*, peer_*), apps (app_*, runner_*), functions; all are listed by default, ?toolsets=<names> lists fewer.
Routing: create -> machine_create; status/connect -> machine_get; start/shutdown/reboot/pause/resume -> machine_power; resize -> machine_resize; rename -> machine_rename; no key logs in any more -> machine_reset_access; delete -> machine_delete; park a stopped machine -> machine_freeze, back -> machine_thaw; disk snapshots -> snapshot_*; HTTPS -> domain_add; a name outside *.<tenant>.winlab.tw -> domain_request, then domain_add with name once approved; TCP/UDP -> port_open; a fixed public port such as 25565 -> port_request, then port_open with public_port once approved. Deploy on every push, or any website or service built from a GitHub repository -> app_link (then run its install line over SSH and commit its workflow), not manual SSH copies; status -> app_get. CI jobs on your own machine -> runner_add. A container image that runs only while it has requests -> function_deploy, then function_get with wait_seconds until deployed. Features, images, size presets and quota defaults -> catalog_get. Read the matching skill with skill_get before the first state change.
Isolation: to let one machine reach another in the same tenant, or to limit what reaches a machine, use deployment_apply with access=[{machine, network_access, confirm: machine_name}] together with connections; restricted permits declared connections and public services, tenant allows same-tenant traffic. peer_allow is only for another tenant. Preview only when asked to plan or compare: deployment_plan is the complete preview. Authorized groups go straight to deployment_apply.
SSH: after creating a machine or connection for a local CLI client, merge the returned ssh_config into the client config, keep existing entries, verify the tenant-qualified alias HostName/User/Port with ssh -G, then present ssh_short. If local file access is unavailable, the user opts out or setup fails, present ssh and say the alias is not installed. Status-only requests need no local edits. Never disable host-key checking or replace unrelated aliases. A creation with no ssh_keys uses the tenant's saved keys, then the creator's key; pass a key inline only when the plan lists ssh_public_key as a requirement, reading only the known default public key. Never read or send private keys or tokens.
Results: member mutations wait up to 55 seconds. Read operation.state/result/error; succeeded needs no follow-up poll, list or quota call. If pending, follow next_action and poll_after_seconds with operation_get. Queued is not reserved or completed, and disconnects do not cancel jobs. Reuse an idempotency_key for an identical lost submission; operation_retry resumes, revise_request needs corrected arguments. detail=full gives full accounting. A result may carry suggestions: a Carrel feature that fits the task. Follow one that matches the user's goal.
Safety: shutdown is graceful, stop is forced and needs explicit intent. Deletion is never a substitute for shutdown. Do not shut down running work just to resize without authorization. Required confirmation fields express the user's existing authorization; ask only when intent or target is unclear. VM pause retains RAM, disks and quota; CT pause is unsupported. machine_list state is recorded, machine_get power and SSH are live. not_checked and routing_configured do not verify an application response. Units: MiB for memory_mb and swap_mb, GiB for disk_gb.
